claim_reviews.basis: Source proves privileged delegation, artifact write, fixed sendEmail integration, read/write authority, and no detected approval/callback controls.
ApplicationIntegrationToolset is statically constrained to integration='sendEmail' and trigger 'api_trigger/send_email'; absence of generic tool_filter does not make this toolset broad.
Outbound authority is through operator-configured MCP_URL and a fixed managed Application Integration target; treating destination scope as absent overclaims egress.
PATH009 depends on the same incorrect unconstrained-egress premise; integration_tool is fixed to the sendEmail integration/trigger.
RemoteA2aAgent is wrapped as AgentTool with no source-visible auth_scheme/auth_credential or approval; source describes canary deploy/promote/rollback authority.
Remote A2A endpoint is operator-configured through CDAGENT_URL; it is dynamic in value but not model-selected/unrestricted.

update_seat only mutates RunContextWrapper[AirlineAgentContext] fields in process/session memory. No external resource mutation is present; data.write and propagated delegated write authority are effective-authority overclaims.
Function tools directly execute requests.get/post/put/delete against model-supplied URL arguments without approval; dynamic egress, external writes, delete, and combined read/write are source-proven.
Runtime Pydantic agent binds a dynamic remote MCP transport with no explicit source-visible tool allowlist.

All four findings arise from repository .mcp.json developer/IDE configuration that is not bound to the application agent. In addition, context7 carries a CONTEXT7_API_KEY header, so the authentication finding is factually incorrect.

recall_gaps.evidence: Six agents and 36 tools are inventoried, but ticket booking/refund/database authority behind ALL_TICKET_TOOLS/delegation yields zero findings; authority relationships remain partial/unresolved.
ToolboxSyncClient.load_toolset('customer_data_tools') is directly bound as Agent tools, but scan reports one agent, zero tools, zero findings.

build_agent() defines model-callable GitHub write, Cloud Build, Artifact Registry, and notification tools, yet scan only models the remote A2A projection and misses local factory/nested tool authority.
get_arcade_tools(..., toolkits=['gmail']) is directly passed to Agent(tools=tools), but scan reports zero tools and zero findings.
StarShell has shell/API/browser/MCP agent factories; scan discovers 19 agents and five MCP servers but only two tools, zero findings, and 18 unresolved-tool diagnostics.
A function creates MCPServerHTTP(url=mcp_server), constructs Agent(..., mcp_servers=[server]), and runs it, but the server is classified unbound/declaration_not_agent_bound.

Twelve MCP relationships are bound to Pydantic agents, including stdio package runners such as video_editor_mcp and serper-mcp-server, but no agent-centric finding represents unresolved/broad MCP tool authority or package execution risk.

design_inferences: Dynamic tool registries must remain first-class bound authority even when the concrete tool catalogue is unresolved.
Function-local Agent factories and nested/local tool definitions need source-scoped normalization rather than top-level-only binding.
Effect semantics must distinguish process/session/context mutation from external/resource data.write.
MCP rules must operate on agent-bound authority relationships; unbound developer configuration remains inventory/coverage, not agent risk.
Dynamic destination values derived from operator configuration and fixed managed integrations must not be treated as arbitrary/model-selected egress.
